Quick recap of the items you asked about:

- Subprocessors: we maintain a current list; attaching the CSV (redwood_subprocessors_20260305.csv) and also include a living link in the DPA.

- Data residency & logging: we support region-specific deployments (US, EU) for Private/Dedicated customers; hosted accounts can be scoped to specific cloud regions on request. Access logs and audit events are retained by default for 30 days; extended retention and S3 export options are available for enterprise plans.

Hi Samuel / Zenith contracts team — quick answers below (quoting the DPA sections where helpful). If you want a tracked-redline DPA, send your markups and we will review.

1) DSR mechanics:
- Controller (Zenith) submits DSRs to privacy@redwood.inference or via the customer console.
- Redwood responds within the timeframe required by applicable law and provides the data exports or confirmation of action. Typical turnaround for standard requests: 30 days; we can agree shorter SLAs in contract for certain enterprise customers.

2) Subprocessors / notice vs consent:
- Redwood maintains a list of subprocessors (attached CSV and linked in the DPA). By default, we provide notice of new subprocessors via the customer portal and email.
- For certain categories (e.g., new subprocessors that will access raw PII storage or key management functions), we are open to explicit consent clauses during negotiation. Please highlight any category you need to control and we will scope it.

3) Breach timing (initial vs full):
- Initial notification: we commit to notifying affected customers within 72 hours of becoming aware of a security incident that impacts customer data. This notification includes known facts and immediate mitigation steps.
- Full incident report: we follow up with a detailed investigation report within 30 days where feasible; if the investigation is ongoing we provide regular updates.
- If Zenith requires an initial notification within 24 hours, we can discuss an SLA amendment for the enterprise contract.

4) Logs & retention / payload handling:
- Standard access logs include: timestamp, request_id, client IP (anonymized option available), model_id, token counts, and response latency.
- Payloads: by default, request and response payloads are not stored persistently for hosted accounts beyond short-lived KV caches used for model context; we retain payloads for up to 24 hours in encrypted caches for debugging/traceability and then purge. Persistent logging of raw payloads (including PII) is disabled by default.
- Customers can enable export of logs to their own S3 (recommended for long-term retention) or configure a longer retention window; we also offer field-level redaction at the API proxy layer for enterprise plans.

Additional links / contacts:
- Subprocessor list (live): https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors/zenith-export-20260305
- Security contact: security@redwood.inference (for incident routing)
- Privacy contact / DSR intake: privacy@redwood.inference

If that addresses your immediate questions, I can prepare a short contract amendment that captures the 72-hour initial notice and the right to request explicit consent for certain subprocessors (or a 30-day notice default). Let me know which parts you want in writing.

Regards,
Dev Patel
